items.title: Macklemore Says US Arenas Won’t Host His Free Palestine Tour
items.summary:
Macklemore says nine major American arenas have refused to book his Free Palestine benefit tour, naming each of them in a lengthy Instagram post. The rapper listed Madison Square Garden, Prudential Center, Barclays Arena, UBS Arena, Intuit Dome, the Kia Forum, Crypto.com Arena, Chase Center and Climate Pledge Arena as venues that offered dates and then withdrew them.

According to his account, as relayed by Stereogum, the venues sent over availability through the end of the year by mid-September, and the openings disappeared once the buildings learned what the shows were for. "The conversations were all different, but the result was the same," Macklemore wrote. "In over twenty years of touring, I've never experienced anything like this."

The tour follows Macklemore's removal from Ed Sheeran's stadium run in September, reportedly at the urging of New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, who did not want Macklemore addressing Israel's war on Palestinians from the stage. The fallout turned sharply against Sheeran, and Macklemore responded by pledging the $1 million he earned from the tour to organizations aiding Palestinians.

He has already staged three benefit shows under the Free Palestine banner, in Dublin, Paris and London. All three sold out and raised money for Palestinian causes, and each brought surprise guests: Hozier and Kneecap in Dublin, Aurora and Pomme in Paris, and Paloma Faith and Aja Monet in London. The American leg was meant to extend that run.

In the post, Macklemore framed the rejections as a question of who controls public speech. "We live in a country that prides itself on freedom of speech," he wrote. "Yet we've reached a point where a handful of billionaires can decide which causes are acceptable, which voices are welcome and which human lives are worth defending. Today it's Palestine. What will it be tomorrow?"

He closed by saying the venues' decision would not change his own: "If they think the threat of never playing another arena in America will make me retreat into silence, they got me fucked up." No US dates for the Free Palestine tour have been announced.

items.title: Future – “Ya Hit” (Feat. Drake, Travis Scott, & Loe Shimmy)
items.summary:
Future has released "Ya Hit," a new single featuring Drake, Travis Scott and Florida rapper Loe Shimmy. ATL Jacob and London Cyr produced the track, which pairs glitchy bass with gothy synth tones.

The song marks another step in the repair of Future and Drake's working relationship. The two have a long shared catalog, including the 2015 joint album What a Time to Be Alive and the No. 1 singles "Way 2 Sexy" and "Wait for U," but that partnership frayed when Future became a key figure in Drake's feud with Kendrick Lamar, who used the Future and Metro Boomin track "Like That" to go after Drake. Future turned up on Drake's Iceman cut "Ran to Atlanta" earlier this year.

"Ya Hit" also reverses course on Future's last release. The Real Me, which arrived in July, carried no guest features at all; Stereogum described the album as messy and forgettable and called the new track the sort of event-style posse cut that has grown rare.

Future, Travis Scott and Loe Shimmy deliver their parts in a chanted cadence that leans toward Playboi Carti's chaotic goth-rap register. Drake takes a different approach, including a veiled jab at an unnamed rival: "Your album ain't gettin' no better/ It's done, so submit it/ You know who gettin' paid the same as your advance?/ My assistant."

The single is out now. Future has not announced whether it belongs to a larger project.

items.title: Tegan and Sara Release New Holiday Songs “I Love Christmas” and “A December to Remember”: Stream
items.summary:
Tegan and Sara have released two new holiday songs, "I Love Christmas" and "A December to Remember." The pair of singles is out now.

The two tracks take different angles on the season. "I Love Christmas" offers a kind of reassurance to listeners who don't share the duo's enthusiasm, with Tegan and Sara promising to love the holiday on their behalf. "A December to Remember" is the more reflective of the two, built around gratitude for the people who make the season worth remembering.

The songs arrive in tandem with Merry Christmess, Tegan Quin's debut middle-grade novel, which was published on September 1st. In a statement cited by Consequence, Quin laid out her credentials: "I'm a Christmas fanatic. I have three Christmas trees. I watch a Christmas movie every single day in December and listen exclusively to Christmas music. Like most sane people, I actually prefer the anticipation of Christmas to Christmas itself. By Christmas afternoon, I'm usually pretty depressed."

The holiday singles follow "Our Year," which the duo released earlier this year and which was their first new music since 2022. Tegan and Sara are also booked as support on Hilary Duff's arena tour in 2027.
